results.statement_role: open conjecture on deterministic convergence of normalised weights
results.reason: Declared conjecture, not a proved result. Its surrounding prose (line 178) adds the simple-edge hypothesis 'no multiple edges linked to node F'; that hypothesis is outside the conjecture environment and must not be imported into the conjecture statement.

results.statement_role: definition of tree-like graph
results.reason: Definition used by Theorem 1.3 and Figure 1 (the cone); carries no proof.

results.statement_role: on tree-like graphs with a simple edge {N,F}, W_a(n)/n tends to 1 and all other normalised weights to 0
results.reason: Author proof is the 15-line prose reduction at lines 668-682: Proposition 2.8 gives W_a(n)/n -> 1, then each other edge incident to N is dominated by the two-edge graph and by the urn map G(x)=x/(x+1-epsilon). Tree monotonicity ('weight of any edge in the tree is always smaller than the weight of the unique edge connected to N on the path to e') supplies the comparison. No new non-routine construction or estimate beyond Corollary 2.2 and Proposition 2.8; assessed below the H2/H3 threshold, hence no separate candidate. The multiplicity-ell remark at line 278 is an asserted direct consequence, not separately proved.
results.owner_disposition: After retaining Proposition2.8, the remaining work is tree-edge domination by its root edge, crossing-probability comparison with the two-edge parallel graph and scalar G(x)=x/(x+1-epsilon) urn domination. Actual668-682 read: no independent H2 construction/estimate beyond these prerequisites; exclusion is based on residual mechanism, not length or main-result status.

results.reason: Author proof at 465-475 is a short closed-set/invariance argument built on Theorem 2.5; used by both new candidates but is a general tool, not a separate core.

results.statement_role: on any finite graph the normalised weights form a stochastic approximation on the convex compact set E, with F Lipschitz on E
results.reason: Author proof at 517-592 (coupling of weighted walks, Green's-function reversibility identity, effective-conductance lower bound via Rayleigh monotonicity, explicit constant K(G)). It is the shared general setup invoked by every example (Theorems 1.3/1.5, Propositions 1.4/1.6). The computation is careful but standard conductance/Green-function bookkeeping, and is not counted as a separate problem-level core; its statements and hypotheses are retained as context.
results.owner_disposition: Finite graph maximal coupling reduces the Lipschitz estimate to reversible Green return ratios; a self-avoiding path and Rayleigh lower bound bound the stopped Green function. Retain as shared authored input; this combination of standard finite-network estimates is below independent H2 here.

results.statement_role: remark that the proof also covers the two variants of the previous paper
results.reason: Unnumbered remark; no separate mathematical content used below.

results.statement_role: if N and F are adjacent, every edge incident to F but not to N has W_e(n)/n -> 0
results.reason: Author proof at 606-665: merge all vertices other than N,F into P with infinite non-terminal weights, bound C_{G(k,l)}(w) <= k(1-w_a)/(k+1-w_a) by Rayleigh monotonicity, compare with a G-urn of G(x)=x/(x+k(1-x)/(k+1-x)) and use G'(0)=(k+1)/k>1. This is a genuine but short conductance-plus-urn lemma; it is reused as step 1 of Proposition 1.4 and as the main input of Theorem 1.3, so it is recorded as a shared support result rather than a separate candidate.
results.owner_disposition: Vertex merging, Rayleigh monotonicity and series/parallel conductance give a single scalar urn drift with derivative(k+1)/k. Retain full606-665 as cone prerequisite; residual network reduction and urn application do not add an independent H2 core.

results.statement_role: for the (p,q)-path graph with min(p,q)>=2, liminf_n W_e(n)/n > c_{p,q} > 0 for every edge e
results.reason: Inside the old proof span [[890,1319]] for 2094; it is the 'retain every path edge' component of the old H2 judgment and must not be split into a new candidate.

results.statement_role: for the (p+q)-path graph, if q>=2 then liminf W_{a_1}(n)/n >= c>0, symmetrically for b_1
results.reason: Base case of Proposition 5.1, inside the 2094 proof span; component, not separate.

results.statement_role: f_p(x)=1-x^p(1-x)/(1-x^p) is a contraction on [0,1] for p>=2
results.reason: Uniqueness component inside the 2094 proof span; component, not separate.

results.reason: Supporting lemma inside the Proposition 1.6 proof span; its proof (1383-1395) uses p_1(w)/w_1 >= 3/2 as w_1->0 and Corollary 2.2.

results.statement_role: signs of F_2 and of F_1(w)w_4-F_4(w)w_1 relative to w_2 versus w_1/(w_1+w_4)
results.reason: Sign lemma used to build the Lyapunov function in Lemma 6.3; part of the Proposition 1.6 proof span.

proof_blocks.notes: Stochastic domination by a modified G_epsilon-urn, then Proposition 2.1.
Coupling estimate, Green's function identity, Rayleigh monotonicity, membership in E.
Reduction to a simple edge by merging parallel edges; graph G(k,l); conductance upper bound; urn comparison.
Formula for P(a_1 reinforced | W(n)); series-conductance lower bound; G(z)=z/(z+1/q).
Proof of Proposition 5.1 by induction; geometric number of crossings; G(x)=x/(x+nu).
Derivative bound via the polynomial phi(x).
Lower bound on p_1(w)/w_1 as w_1->0.
Sign of F_2 from the displayed F_2 formula; ordering inequality for the two weights; displayed difference of quotients.
Lyapunov function h=max(|u|,|v|); reduction to w_2=w_1/(w_1+w_4)=1/2; then w_3->1/2; then uniqueness of w* from the cubic.

prose_proof_ranges.notes: Section 3 has no proof environment; the whole section body is the author proof. It uses Proposition 2.8 and the two-edge domination (3.1).

Section 4 body: stochastic-approximation setup for E'; computation of p_1,p_2 and F; Step 1 (Prop 2.8); Step 2 (Phi/Psi and reflected random walk); Step 3 (ODE zeros and sign regions); Step 4 (Corollary 2.6).

Section 5 body excluding subsection headers and the three proof environments; ends at 1319 with the conclusion of Theorem 1.5. Together with proof_blocks 5.1/5.2/5.3 this is the old 2094 proof range [[890,1319]].
Section 6 body plus the appendix derivation of the displayed p_1,p_2,p_3 formulas. The appendix is the author's own calculation of p_1,p_2,p_3; without it those formulas would be unproved.
